title: A run stopped at its ceiling counts toward the loop's failure stop
body:
## Summary
runLoop counts a ceiling-stopped run as one of maxFailures, so three runs that hit their cost ceiling end the loop as failure-stopped, reported as "3 topics ended failed".

## Description
lib/articles/loop.ts:15-21 lists failure-stopped as "maxFailures topics ended failed (each already resumed maxResumes times)" and ceiling-stopped as per run, "marked for a human and never resumed". The worker's ceiling branch (lib/articles/loop.ts `one`, the `ceiling !== undefined` branch) does `failures++`, and a halted run does too. So a ceiling run, never resumed, is counted where the header says only runs resumed maxResumes times are, and the loop's stop reason names failures that were ceilings. Fixed means either the header says ceilings count toward the failure stop, or ceilings are tallied apart (their own stop, or none). Which one is the operator's call: it changes when a nightly --loop stops spending.

## Flow
- runLoop with maxFailures 1 and a ceiling under a run's price (articles-loop probe "a run over its cost ceiling") -> report.stop failure-stopped, report.runs[0].end ceiling-stopped
- the reason line says "1 topics ended failed" for a run that did not fail

## Expected impact
The operator reading loop.json learns the loop stopped on ceilings, not failures, or the loop keeps going past ceiling runs. Could break: a loop that today stops after three runaway runs would keep launching.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the stop reason names what stopped the loop
Before: 1 of 1 ceiling-stopped runs counted as a failure; stop failure-stopped (articles-loop probe, cost ceiling case)
After: unmeasured - two designs, the choice is which number the operator wants a ceiling to move
Method: probe - the existing ceiling case reproduces the Before; the After depends on the decision
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence: lib/articles/loop.ts:15-21 (header), lib/articles/lib/articles/loop.ts:474-475 `row.end = "ceiling-stopped"; failures++;`, tests/golden-path/articles-loop.probe.spec.ts "a run over its cost ceiling" expects stop failure-stopped

title: The loop's run ceilings and run estimate are literals beside the run price hint
body:
## Summary
DEFAULT_CEILINGS (120 USD / 30 USD / 45 turns) and DEFAULT_EST_RUN_USD (70) in lib/articles/loop.ts are written by hand next to a comment quoting the measured band that types.ts RUN_COST_HINT holds as data (47-92 USD, 26-32 turns).

## Description
fleet-orchestration/soft-budget-under-the-hard-cap: "the two numbers must be derived from one source" - a soft number and a hard cap written separately drift the first time either is tuned. types.ts:486 RUN_COST_HINT is the one spelling of a run's price (its own comment: "a second spelling of a price is how two surfaces come to disagree"), but loop.ts:232-236 restates its figures in prose and sets the ceilings and the estimate as independent literals. When RUN_COST_HINT moves (it says it will, when the model or roster changes), the loop's estimate and ceilings stay. Fixed: ceilings and estimate derived from RUN_COST_HINT (e.g. ceiling = usdHigh x margin, turns = turnsHigh + margin, estimate = midpoint), with the margins named.

## Flow
- RUN_COST_HINT.usdHigh is raised to 110 after a roster change
- DEFAULT_CEILINGS.runUsd stays 120: a normal run now sits within 10 USD of its ceiling
- the fix: derive the three numbers, pin the derivation in the loop probe

## Expected impact
Ceilings follow the measured price. It changes the numbers that stop paid runs (70 -> 69.5 for the estimate under a midpoint rule), so it is the operator's call.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one source for a run's price and the limits set from it
Before: 4 hand literals (120, 30, 45, 70) beside 4 data figures, 0 derived
After: 0 literals not derived, under margins the operator picks
Method: probe - counted on the tree; the After needs the margins
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-loosen

body:
## Summary

## Description
The header (lib/imaging/safeUrl.ts:25-27) says the resolved check is done 'at connect time, because a name under an attacker's control can point anywhere and can be changed between two lookups'. A hostname with a zero TTL that answers public first and 127.0.0.1 / 169.254.169.254 second passes the check and connects to the private address. Fixed looks like: validation inside the socket's lookup (an undici `Agent({ connect: { lookup } })` dispatcher passed to fetch) so the address checked is the address connected to; the pre-flight check can stay for the literal/scheme rules. ## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the address validated is the address connected to
Before: two lookups per hop; the second unchecked (read from the code; no probe can drive it without a dispatcher seam)
After: one lookup per hop, inside connect; a rebinding resolver is refused
Method: simulation - the platform fetch's internal lookup cannot be injected without adding an undici dispatcher, which is the change itself

title: The migration failure mark is written after a step fails, not before it runs
body:
## Summary
migrations:error-propagation asks for a failed-at mark 'set before the step runs, cleared only by its success'; migrate.ts writes it only after a step reports failure, so a process that dies mid-step leaves no mark.

## Description
packages/kernel/src/migrate.ts:197-203 writes the mark in its own tx after the step tx returns an error. A step that kills the process (OOM on a table rebuild, a native crash, a kill during a long boot) rolls back and leaves nothing: every next boot re-runs it, crash-looping with no record of which step. The registry map already records this as the pair's deviation (2026-10-19). Fixed: insert the mark (reason 'in progress') in its own tx before the step and DELETE it inside the step's tx; the existing failure path overwrites it with the real reason. Depends on the operator door card above: once a kill mid-migration strands the store, clearing must be one command.

## Flow
- boot -> migrate -> step k tx -> process killed
- next boot: no mark, step k re-runs, dies again
- fix: mark before, clear in the step's own transaction; crash.ts-driven test kills a child mid-step and asserts the mark stands

## Expected impact
A crash-looping migration names its step on the next boot instead of looping silently. Could break: an interrupted dev boot now needs the clear command (the trade the technique accepts).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a step that kills its process leaves a standing, named mark
Before: 0 marks after a child process is killed inside a step (by construction: the mark is written only on a returned error)

title: A damaged blob cannot be healed by putting its bytes again
body:
## Summary
blob.put() returns ok without writing when a file of the right SIZE already sits at the address, so a blob read() reports as damaged stays damaged however often the source bytes are put again.

## Description
packages/kernel/src/blob.ts:90 short-circuits on size; :120 read() re-hashes and returns internal 'does not hash to its name; the file is damaged'. Bit rot or a hand edit that keeps the length leaves a file put() will never replace. Fixed: put() keeps the size fast path, but when read() has reported damage (or on an explicit `repair`), it rewrites through tmp + rename; or put() compares a hash of the existing file when sizes match and the file is small. The cost of hashing hundreds of MB on every idempotent put is the reason this is not Lane A.

## Flow
- put(bytes) -> file at address
- a same-length corruption of the file
- read(ref) -> internal damaged
- put(bytes) again -> ok, file unchanged; read still damaged

## Expected impact
A damaged media blob can be restored from its source. Could break: put latency on large files if the check is unconditional.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a damaged blob is repairable
Before: 0 of 1 damaged blobs healed by re-put (walked blob.ts:90)
After: 1 of 1, with put latency on an undamaged 100 MB blob measured on both arms
Method: simulation - walked put/read; the test is S but the design choice (hash on put vs a repair verb) is the arm to measure
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none

title: slottedIn counts a dry-published slot as placed, though a dry publication holds nothing
body:
## Summary
slottedIn reads a plan's slot part as placed when a slot for it is scheduled, publishing or published - including published DRY - while every other holder rule says a dry publication holds nothing.

## Description
packages/kernel/src/slots/read.ts:105 `SELECT 1 ... WHERE part_id = ? AND state IN ('scheduled', 'publishing', 'published')` has no `dry = 0`; its docstring (read.ts:98-103) defines placed as a slot that HOLDS its item. clashOf (core.ts:82) and the index slots_one_holder (schema.ts step 4) both say a dry-published slot holds nothing (the L62 ruling). So a project whose slot part went out only as a rehearsal reads its slot part ratified and the project shipped. Which is right is a product call: excluding dry makes a dry-launched project never ratify its slot part; keeping it makes 'shipped' mean 'rehearsed'.

## Flow
- compose + launch a project in dry mode, its slot part's slot published dry
- slottedIn -> true; the part reads ratified; listProjects groups the project 'shipped'

## Expected impact
The Projects shelf's 'shipped' group can hold projects nothing was published for. Could break: a dry rehearsal of a whole project that today completes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one definition of 'holds an item' across the calendar
Before: 2 of 3 holder rules exclude a dry publication (clashOf, slots_one_holder); slottedIn does not
After: 3 of 3, or the docstring names the exemption
Method: probe - read the three rules; the behaviour is a direction choice, not a measurement
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
packages/kernel/src/slots/read.ts:98-106
packages/kernel/src/slots/core.ts:82-84

title: SoundError statuses map to two different AppErrorCode tables in batch.ts and arrange.ts
body:
## Summary

## Description

## Flow

- the same 404 through Arrange -> 'not-found'

One taxonomy for the store's refusals; a UI that branches on code reads the same thing from both doors. Could break: a caller keyed on batch's 'conflict'.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one SoundError -> AppErrorCode table
Before: 2 tables, 5 of 7 statuses disagree
After: 1 table, 0
Method: probe - counted from the two sources; the right code per 409 needs the store's 409s split first
Result: better

title: The image gate's hold ignores the request's size and holds $0 when no image row is priced
body:
## Summary
holdFor's image hold is dearestRate('image') x units: the 1K Google figure whatever size the request pins, and $0 if no image row were priced.

## Description
quote() refuses to carry the 1K figure to a 2K render ('a fiction'), but the pre-call gate does exactly that, so a 2K or 4K Google batch is held at roughly half or a quarter of what it costs. And if every image row went unpriced or dated out, dearestRate is undefined and the hold is $0 - 'unpriced is not free' broken at the gate. Holding more is a tightening, but the figure for 2K is unmeasured: choosing a multiplier, or refusing sized requests, is inventing a price or changing what is offered. v1 (lib/imaging/budget.ts estimatePendingUsd) has the same rule.

## Flow
- image generate, size 2K, units 4
- hold 4 x $0.045 = $0.18
- vendor bills roughly 2x per size step

## Expected impact
The imaging ceiling would hold what a sized batch costs. Could break: a hold that refuses work the ceiling would in fact fit.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the gate never holds less than a call can cost
Before: sized requests held at the 1K rate; no-row case holds $0
After: operator's rule: a measured 2K row, a declared multiplier, or a refusal
Method: simulation - walked holdFor and dearestRate; the missing figure is a price nobody measured
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
packages/kernel/src/router/reserve.ts holdFor image: `dearest === undefined ? 0 : dearest.usdPerUnit * Math.max(req.units, 1)`
packages/kernel/src/pricing/quote.ts dearestRate ignores atSize; PRICE_TABLE google gemini-3.1-flash-image atSize 1K $0.045 ('Nano Banana roughly doubles per size step', quote.ts header)

title: An estimated (priced) Gemini turn books no spend row: the ledger counts only the seat
body:
## Summary
spend.ts books only `vendor-reported` costs; Google's adapter prices with priceTurn (basis `estimated`), so the only real-money engine never writes a $ row, even on a priced model.

## Description
lib/text/spend.ts bookServedTurn: `const vendor = p.costBasis === "vendor-reported" && finite(p.costUsd)` - an estimated cost becomes `unpriced` and bumps a counter. providers/google.ts passes `quote.basis` (estimated whenever a row has rates, today gemini-3.8-flash; every in-service row is unpriced). The operator's memory says only Gemini is real cost, and the claude seat's total_cost_usd is notional - so the ledger books the notional figure and refuses the real one. cost-metering 'estimate before, measure after, track the gap' says the estimate is a row with its basis, not nothing. Booking estimates (basis 'estimate') changes what the text-usd window totals mean - an operator decision on a count-only class (2026-10-07 'Count only, refuse nothing').

## Flow
- a priced Google turn serves with costBasis estimated
- bookServedTurn books unpriced
- text-usd spent excludes it

## Expected impact
Gemini spend becomes visible in the window. Could break: any reader that treats text-usd spent as vendor-reported only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the real-money engine appears in its ledger
Before: 0 $ rows for an estimated Google turn
After: 1 row basis estimate
Method: probe - text-spend card case 4 already shows an unpriced google turn booking 0 rows
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-loosen
evidence: lib/text/spend.ts bookServedTurn vendor test; lib/text/providers/google.ts quote.basis; lib/text/pricing.ts priceTurn basis 'estimated'
